texts.preamble: Radhey Lal vs State Of U.P. on 15 November, 2019 Author: Manju Rani Chauhan Bench: Manju Rani Chauhan High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad ?Court No. - 78 Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 49442 of 2019 Applicant :- Radhey Lal
texts.facts: The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-Radhey Lal with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No. 560 of 2019, under Section 60A Excise Act and Section 272 I.P.C., Police Station-Munda pandey, District-Moradabad, during the pendency of the trial. The first information report has been lodged by the Police on 25th September, 2019 against the applicant with the allegation that on 25th September, 2019 at 05:00 p.m. when the informant and other Police personnels were checking the suspicious vehicles and miscreants to maintain law and order, one informer informed him that one person used to prepare adulterated liquors by mixing urea and sell the same on higher rates at Mankara crossing near bye-pass. On believing the said information, the informant and other Police personnels after completing all legal formalities Radhey Lal vs State Of U.P. on 15 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148198100/ 1 reached old closed factory near the Manakara crossing and saw that a person was preparing adulterated liquors. After surrounding the said person, the Police caught him. Five litres of adulterated liquors and machines of preparing adulterated liquors are alleged to have been recovered from the possession of the applicant.
texts.arguments: It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive. False and fabricated prosecution story has been made by the police. The alleged recovery is planted one by the Police. There is no independent or public witness from the basis of which it can be said that the applicant is involved in the commission of the alleged offence. There is no chemical analysis report from which it can be said that the alleged recovered material is adulterated liquors. It has further been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been enacted by the legislature and hence the implication of the applicant under Sections 272, 273 I.P.C. is unjustified. Offence under Section 60/63 of Excise Act is bailable and triable by the Magistrate. The applicant has one criminal antecedents to his credit except the present one but the same has satisfactorily been explained in paragraph-12 of the affidavit filed in support of the present bail application. It is next contended that there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the witnesses and in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail. The applicant is in jail since 25th September, 2019. Per contra learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant but he could not dispute the factual submissions as urged by the learned counsel for the applicant. Considering the the nature of the offence, material/evidence brought on record, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties as well as the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh Versus State of U.P. and another, reported in (2018) 3 SCC 22, let the applicant involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the following conditions:- (i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
